If Δ > 0, there are two real solutions: x = [-b ± √Δ] / 2a. If Δ = 0, there's one real solution: x = -b/2a. If Δ < 0, there are two complex solutions. Always check your solutions by substituting back into the original equation. This systematic approach reflects my conscientious nature.

First, find the derivative f'(x). Set f'(x) = 0 and solve for x values - these are potential stationary points.
